desc:
The diameter of a binary tree is the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes. The path may or may not pass through the root, and it is allowed to turn at a node (go up, then down). A tree with zero or one node has diameter 0.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] the answer is 3, for example the path 4 → 2 → 1 → 3.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Look at the highest node of the longest path. Where can that path turn around?
If a path peaks at node x, it goes down into the left subtree and down into the right subtree. Its length is the (deepest chain in left) + (deepest chain in right).
Compute subtree heights bottom-up. At every node, the best path peaking there is heightLeft + heightRight (heights counted in nodes). Keep the maximum of that over all nodes.
editorial: Every path has exactly one highest node, the place where it turns (or an endpoint). If the path peaks at x, the best choice is to go as deep as possible on each side, so the longest path peaking at x has height(left) + height(right) edges, where height counts nodes and a missing child has height 0.

So one bottom-up pass is enough: compute the height of every node from its children's heights and update a global best with hl + hr. The answer is that best value. The array encoding lets you do the pass backwards over the real nodes without any recursion.
